failures.criterion: Change: a stored document renders it back so that it reads the same (spec); T2 image-address writer (plan)
failures.evidence: An image address that ends in a backslash is written as it stands by escapeImageSource (render.go:796-817: it doubles a backslash only when the next byte of the address is ASCII punctuation), so the final backslash escapes the `)` or `>` the writer adds and both Go and the engine read `![a](u\)` as the text `![a](u)`. On the real surface: in the browser-suite stack at 49260f10, `dispatch artifact --project TPR --name slash.md --content '![a](https://a.example/u\\)'` (CommonMark for the address `https://a.example/u\`, which Go and the engine both read so) exits 1 with `markdown is not a Proof document: outside Proof schema: the markdown the document would be stored as reads back otherwise (a paragraph reads back holding "![a](https://a.example/u\\)", not "")`; a browser edit setting such an address is refused the same way. Red test (commit 8ea780a2): `cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/ -count=1 -run TestAnImageAddressEndingInABackslashRendersAndReadsBack` (bun on PATH) -> FAIL on 5 of 6 rows (`u\` and `u\\` plain, `<u v\>` angle, both in a table cell); the row with a title after the address passes. The base 4bbb2a9c has the same defect (my probe failed the same rows there), but it is in the writer this change rewrites, the escape that makes an address read back, and the deployment rule is to fix an adjacent defect now. Checked satisfiable: changing that condition to `char == '\\' && (index+1 == len(src) || isASCIIPunctuation(src[index+1]))` makes the red test, TestReferencesInEveryValueRenderAndReadBackInBothParsers, TestReferenceSpellingsThatReadBackRenderUnchanged and TestRenderReadsBackInBothParsersAsTheEditorShowsIt pass (change reverted; not committed).
